title: Salisbury Steak with Gravy, Potatoes, Vegetables (Frozen Meal)

content.title: About
content.content: Salisbury steak with gravy is a ready‑to‑heat frozen meal that includes a seasoned beef patty in a savory gravy, boiled potatoes, and a mixed vegetable medley. It is designed for quick preparation in a microwave or on the stovetop, delivering a complete meal in just a few minutes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish was first introduced in the United States in the 1950s as a convenient home‑style dinner.
Salisbury steak is named after Dr. James H. Salisbury, an early 20th‑century physician who promoted the recipe for its nutritional value.
Typical ingredients include ground beef, onion, carrot, and seasonings, with a gravy made from beef broth and tomato paste.
Modern frozen versions retain flavor through rapid blast‑freezing technology.
Each package is usually a single serving (about 300‑350 g).

items.title: Protein
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and vegetables supply B6 and B12 vitamins, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium, which helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Dietary Fiber
items.content: The vegetable mix adds fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Beef contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: Prepared frozen meals often contain added salt; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: To extend shelf life, some products include food preservatives that may not be suitable for everyone.

items.title: Beef Allergy
items.content: Although rare, some people may be allergic to beef or to seasoning ingredients.

items.title: Heating Requirements
items.content: Insufficient heating can leave live bacteria; follow the recommended time and temperature guidelines.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Remove the meal from its packaging, heat in the microwave or on the stovetop until the internal temperature reaches at least 75 °C (167 °F). Serve immediately; garnish with fresh herbs or a splash of sauce if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen meal at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once opened, consume within 24 hours if stored in the refrigerator. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
